title: Uninvestment Check
concept: A short, honest count to tell needing space apart from pulling away — so you know which repair to reach for. It describes behaviour you can both see, never your partner’s intent.
whenToUse: When warmth is missing even in ordinary moments, repairs feel like going through the motions, you’ve stopped planning ahead together, or contempt has replaced frustration.
steps: Each of you marks, on your own, which of the eight signs (listed under Practise) you’ve noticed, then share. Describe behaviour you’ve seen — don’t claim to know the other person’s intent.
If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. The same goes for fear or coercion at any count.
None of these? Good. Keep up the daily floor. With one or two signs, it likely needs space and small repairs (Micro-Repair, Morning + Evening Rhythm).

Three or more signs: one or both of you may be pulling away. Book a Full Recovery conversation within a week. For drift, no one “caused” it: you both name your part. (A specific breach of trust goes to Trust Recovery instead.)
Set a time window to check whether you’re both leaning back in.

phrases.text: I’m noticing some distance. Do you just need space, or is something bigger going on?
I want a Full Recovery conversation. Can we book it for when we’re both calm?
Contempt means we can’t just carry on as normal.

working: A ticks three signs and B ticks four. They overlap on fewer messages, talk that’s all logistics, and repairs that feel routine. They book a Full Recovery conversation within a week, then keep up their morning and evening check-ins for 21 days, looking back once a week.
notWorking: Dinners have gone quiet, and one of you decides to wait for the other “to miss me”. A month goes by with nothing booked, and the quiet starts to feel normal.
activity: Mark the signs on your own, then compare. Check monthly, or weekly if you’re worried. The eight signs: (1) fewer non-logistical check-ins, (2) less curiosity about each other, (3) avoiding future plans, (4) doing more on your own in place of shared time (time apart is healthy), (5) mostly practical conversations, (6) going-through-the-motions affection, (7) repairs that feel routine, (8) contempt instead of frustration. If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. Then use the steps above to see what your count means.
warn: If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. Fear or coercion at any count: stop; safety and outside support come first.
note: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
